step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Monzo's core banking payment processing platform on AWS. The journey begins when a user taps a card at a payment terminal, sending transaction details through third-party payment schemes into Monzo's physical data centers and over AWS Direct Connect into the AWS cloud. Inside Amazon EKS, the transaction first hits the Tokenization Microservice to strip sensitive credit card details. The request then flows to the Cards Microservice (verifying card status against the Cards Table in Amazon Keyspaces), the Account Microservice (verifying account linkage against the Account Table in Keyspaces), and the Ledger Microservice (performing double-entry bookkeeping calculations). Once validated, a synchronous authorization response travels back down through Direct Connect to the terminal. AWS WAF, Application Load Balancer, and AWS Nitro Enclaves provide security and runtime isolation across the infrastructure.

graph.name: Monzo Core Banking Platform Architecture
graph.notes: Monzo processes millions of synchronous payment transactions using Amazon EKS microservices and Amazon Keyspaces for low-latency NoSQL state persistence.

edges.notes: Customer taps card at terminal, sending payment details through scheme
Payment network routes transaction into Monzo's Direct Connect
Direct Connect routes payload into Tokenization Microservice on EKS
Tokenized request passed to Cards Microservice for card validation
Cards Microservice queries Cards Table in Keyspaces
Account Microservice reads account state from Keyspaces
Request passes to Ledger Microservice for balance check
Synchronous authorization result returned back out through Direct Connect
